result.title: Context-Shielded Backdoor Attack against Large Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) routinely use inference-time visual-token compression to prune hundreds of patch tokens down to a compact budget. Existing LVLM backdoors fire whenever a triggered image appears, whereas prior deployment-triggered attacks activate only when model weights are quantized or pruned. However, conventional LVLM backdoors exhibit nearly 100% attack success rate (ASR) under full-token inference, immediately exposing compromised checkpoints during pre-deployment auditing. We reveal context stripping: surrounding clean visual tokens suppress an embedded trigger at full length, whereas token pruning strips this context away and activates the backdoor. Motivated by this finding, we propose StripWake, a projector-only backdoor that remains dormant under full-token auditing yet activates across unseen compressors. Specifically, StripWake pairs clean-supervised full-token views with target-supervised randomized compressed views, and aligns early visual attention with a frozen benign teacher to preserve clean utility. On LLaVA-1.5-7B across nine unseen compressors, StripWake stays dormant at 0.4% full-token ASR yet achieves 94.0%-99.7% compressed ASR across five primary compressors without CIDEr loss.

AI.brief_summary: 论文揭示「上下文剥离」现象：全长度视觉 token 中的干净上下文会压制植入的触发器，而推理期视觉 token 压缩会剥离该上下文并激活后门；据此提出只在 projector 上注入、在全 token 审计下休眠而在多种未见压缩器下激活的后门 StripWake，并用全 token 干净监督视图与随机压缩目标视图配对、向冻结良性教师对齐早期视觉注意力来保持干净性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作表明视觉 token 预算的改变会实质改变内部视觉信息是否被使用，这一线索可供核查 LVR 中「模型是否真正依赖被压缩保留的视觉证据」以及 token 压缩作为评估混淆因素的问题，其双视图配对与注意力对齐也可作为跨 token 预算监督的参考。
